Architectural Design Overview 2.1 Design Philosophy & Patterns The platform architecture utilizes a distributed, decoupled structural model. This ensures a clean separation of concerns between raw client data collection, state processing, and data persistence layers. 2.1.1 Microservices & Layered Approaches Layered Pattern: The backend engine isolates network transport wrappers from internal domain calculations. This ensures business engine computations function independently of protocol layers like HTTP or WebSockets. Singleton Pattern: Database management pools and memory store clients are structured as singleton engines. This avoids connection leaks and safeguards state pools under heavy client volumes. 2.2 Subsystem Decomposition (Block Diagram) The system runtime topology consists of three primary, decoupled technical environments: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ CLIENT LAYER (PRESENTATION) │ │ [Web Portal Node] ──(HTTPS/TLS 1.3)───> [Mobile Application Bundle] │ └──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ LOGIC LAYER (PROCESSING) │ │ [API Gateway Engine] ─────────────────> [Asynchronous Task Worker] │ └──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ STORAGE LAYER (PERSISTENCE) │ │ [Relational DB Primary] ──────────────> [In-Memory Cache Cluster] │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 2.3 Component Hardware Blueprint Client Machines: Consumer hardware configurations running v8 layout engines with a minimum memory pool allocations of 2GB RAM. Application Compute Instance: Isolated container instances provisioned with 2 Virtual CPUs, 4GB System Memory, and an expandable 40GB SSD cluster node. Database Host Engine: Dedicated managed data node provisioned with 1 Virtual CPU, 2GB Dedicated System Memory, and write-ahead configuration frameworks. 3. Detailed Subsystem Design 3.1 API & Logic Routing Subsystem 3.1.1 Behavioral Specifications The logic engine intercepts client calls, unpacks secure payloads, runs integrity scripts, and schedules operations across persistent database pools. 3.1.2 Dynamic Processing Flow (Sequence Trace) The diagram below maps how processing flows when a user uploads transaction blocks to the platform core: Client App API Gateway Task Worker Data Cluster │ │ │ │ │ ─── Submit Payload ────────>│ │ │ │ │ ── Push to Queue ──────>│ │ │ │ │ ── Write Records ────>│ │ <── Return HTTP 202 ────────│ │ │ 3.2 Client View & Presentation Interface 3.2.1 Navigation Layout Logic The web application initializes into a single-page engine frame. It tracks routing states on client processing chains to prevent reload loops. 3.2.2 Form Validation Rules Client Checking: Form modules parse fields against regular expressions before triggering network serialization scripts. Backend Sanitization: Server endpoints re-validate fields against schema rules to catch any modified payload attempts. 4. Database & Storage Architecture 4.1 Logical Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) The entity schema relies on explicit relational structures to guarantee data integrity across transaction cycles. ┌─────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ ACCOUNT │ │ TRANSACTION_RECORD │ ├─────────────────┤ ├────────────────────────┤ │ PK id (UUID) │1 ─────────── 0*│ PK id (UUID) │ │ email │ │ FK account_id (UUID) │ │ hash_pass │ │ amount_cents │ └─────────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘ 4.2 Physical Data Dictionary Sheets 4.2.1 Data Table: ACCOUNT Field Identifier Data Type Variant Constraint Profiles Target System Description id UUID PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL Global unique identification hash. email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE, INDEX, NOT NULL Authenticated corporate user profile address. hash_pass VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL Salted blowfish encryption string representation. 4.2.2 Data Table: TRANSACTION_RECORD Field Identifier Data Type Variant Constraint Profiles Target System Description id UUID PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL Unique sequential record identification string. account_id UUID FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES ACCOUNT(id) Traceability index back to creator account. amount_cents BIGINT NOT NULL, DEFAULT 0 Financial field tracked explicitly in lowest denomination. 5. Interface & Integration Specifications 5.1 RESTful Endpoint Protocols 5.1.1 Account Authentication Token Dispatch Protocol Verb: POST System Location Path: /api/v1/auth/token Request Payload Scheme (JSON): { "email": "student@faculty.edu", "password": "SecurePasswordString" } Success Status Code Responses: 200 OK Success Output Payload (JSON): { "token_type": "Bearer", "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", "expires_in_seconds": 900 } Error Failure Status Options: 401 Unauthorized (Invalid credentials), 429 Too Many Requests (Rate threshold exceeded). 5.2 External System Third-Party Integrations Identity Provider Platform: Communication over OAuth 2.0 servers to verify academic registration profiles. Storage Backup Target: Cron systems executing shell tasks to upload compressed, encrypted database records onto external faculty network storage mounts. 6. Security & Cryptographic Blueprints 6.1 Encryption & Key Infrastructure In-Flight Protections: All network traffic routes through secure transport tunnels running HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS). Storage Protection Configurations: Sensitive credentials utilize environment variable stores injected at application runtime.
